passage: The village of Espen Cross will lose its last bank branch in February, when Cortland Savings closes the office it has kept on the green since 1928. The bank cited a fall in counter transactions, down 62 percent in ten years, and said the nearest branch will now be in Weldon, eleven miles away by the valley road. A cash machine will remain in the wall of the old building for at least three years under an agreement with the parish council, and the mobile post office, which visits on Tuesdays and Fridays, will add basic banking services from March. Shopkeeper Una Ferris, who banks her takings daily, told the council she would now have to close her store for an hour each morning to make the drive. The branch employs three people; the bank says two have accepted transfers and one is retiring. The council has written to two rival banks asking whether either would take on the premises, and one, Halvard and Company, has agreed to a site visit in January. The building itself is protected and cannot be altered outside without consent.
question: In what year did Cortland Savings open its Espen Cross branch?

passage: The Delft Street swimming pool will reopen on the first of June after a winter closure that stretched to fourteen months, the recreation board confirmed on Thursday. The pool shut in April of last year for what was planned as a twelve week replacement of its filtration plant, but workers then found the main tank's concrete shell cracked along the deep end, a defect traced to a repair done cheaply in 1996. Fixing the shell added 480,000 dollars to the original 220,000 dollar budget and required draining the tank twice. The board covered the overrun with an insurance recovery, a loan against next year's budget, and 74,000 dollars raised by the Friends of the Pool through swimming galas held at the college pool in Rothbury. Season passes will cost the same as two years ago, and pass holders from the lost season get a 40 percent discount. The board also confirmed the pool will finally heat its water with the rink's waste heat, piped under the car park, a scheme first proposed in 2009 and shelved twice. Opening day includes a relay attempt on the club's 1985 record.
question: How much did fixing the cracked concrete shell add to the pool project's cost?

passage: A cargo van carrying 4,000 loaves of bread overturned on the Kestrel Pass road early on Wednesday, closing the eastbound lane for five hours and filling the morning air, by several accounts, with the smell of a bakery. The driver, who works for the Ovenbird bread company, swerved to avoid a fallen branch near the summit and put two wheels into the soft shoulder, tipping the van against the rock face. He was checked at the scene and drove away in the recovery truck, unhurt apart from a bruised shoulder. About a third of the load, protected in sealed crates, was salvaged and donated to the food bank in Tarrow, which said the gift amounted to roughly 1,300 loaves, its largest single donation of the year. The rest was written off. The pass road reopened at 11 a.m. once the van was winched upright and the shoulder gravel swept. The highway office noted it was the fourth incident at that bend in two years and said a warning sign and a guard rail extension were already scheduled for the summer program, at a cost near 22,000 dollars.
question: How many loaves of bread went to the food bank in Tarrow?

passage: The observatory on Mount Carden will stay open after all. The university announced on Friday that a consortium of three amateur astronomy societies will take over nightly operations under a ten year lease, ending eighteen months of uncertainty that began when the physics department withdrew its funding. The societies will pay a token rent of one dollar a year but must cover utilities and insurance, estimated together at 54,000 dollars annually, and must open the main dome to the public at least 80 nights a year. The 36 inch reflector, installed in 1962, remains university property and will still be available to faculty for up to 30 nights a season by arrangement. Consortium chair Nils Adeyemi said membership across the three societies stands at about 400 and that a volunteer roster of 60 trained operators has already been drawn up. The visitor program will keep its popular winter lecture series, though the planetarium projector, which failed in March, will not be repaired; a grant application for a digital replacement, costed at 90,000 dollars, went in last month. The first public night under the new arrangement is set for the autumn equinox.
question: How many nights a year must the main dome be open to the public?

passage: Egg prices at the Norham weekly market have doubled since spring, and stallholders point to a single cause: the fox that has worked its way through the poultry yards of the river villages since April. The county's animal control office has logged 34 confirmed raids on henhouses across seven villages, with losses passing 900 birds, and believes one unusually bold animal is responsible for most of them, based on tracks and on the pattern of raids occurring in early evening rather than at night. Two farms have installed electric fencing with grants from the agricultural board, which covers 60 percent of the cost, and neither has been raided since. A trapping effort in May caught three foxes, none of them, the office concedes, likely the right one, since raids continued without pause. The office now recommends fencing over trapping and has scheduled demonstrations at the market on the next two Saturdays. Meanwhile the price of a dozen eggs has gone from 3 dollars to 6 dollars, and the market's egg stalls have dropped from five to two. One stallholder, Berta Klimova, now drives her eggs in from her sister's farm forty miles inland.
question: How many confirmed henhouse raids has the animal control office logged?

passage: The town orchestra of Villard has appointed its first resident conductor in 21 years, choosing the 34 year old violist Renate Okonjo from a field of 87 applicants. Okonjo, who has led the ensemble twice as a guest, takes up the post in September on a three year contract and will conduct six of the season's nine concerts, with guests taking the rest. The orchestra, an amateur body of about 70 players founded in 1911, has been led since 2003 by a rotation of guest conductors, an arrangement the committee said produced fine single concerts but no sustained direction. The appointment panel heard final auditions over one weekend, giving each of three finalists a two hour rehearsal with the full orchestra; players then voted, and the committee confirmed their preference unanimously. Okonjo has said she wants the orchestra to commission a short new work every season, beginning with a fanfare for the town's 900th anniversary next year, and to restart the youth mentoring scheme that lapsed during the pandemic years. Her opening program pairs a symphony the orchestra last played in 1987 with a suite by a composer born in Villard itself.
question: How many applicants applied for the resident conductor post?

passage: A kayaker stranded overnight on a gravel bar in the Sorrel River was lifted to safety at dawn on Sunday by a helicopter crew, ending a search that began when his empty car was found at the Pike Hollow put-in. The man, a 29 year old from Grenfield, had set out alone on Saturday morning intending to run the eleven mile stretch to the Weavers Ford takeout. High water from Friday's rain pushed him past his takeout, and when his kayak wrapped on a strainer near dusk he swam to the bar, losing the boat but keeping his dry bag. Inside were a foil blanket, a headlamp, and a whistle, which searchers on the bank heard at about 5 a.m. The county rescue coordinator, Imre Fontaine, said the whistle shortened the search by hours, since the river corridor there runs deep between wooded bluffs and the man's phone had gone down with the kayak. He was treated for mild hypothermia at the scene and released without a hospital stay. The river was running at roughly three times its usual summer volume. It was the unit's sixth river call this year, against nine in all of last year.
question: What sound led searchers to the stranded kayaker?

passage: The Petrel Point seabird count, taken every June since 1974, recorded 11,400 breeding pairs of terns this year, the highest figure in the count's history and nearly double the low of 6,100 pairs reached in 2016. Wardens credit the recovery to three measures introduced together five years ago: a seasonal ban on dogs along the nesting beach, a string of decoy colonies with solar powered callers that draw birds away from the eroding west spit, and sustained trapping of rats on the point, which removed over 600 animals in the first two winters alone. The count also logged 240 pairs of oystercatchers, steady on recent years, and, for the first time since 1988, a single pair of skimmers, which fledged two young in July. Not all news was good: the gull colony on the outer stack fell by a fifth, a decline the wardens link to poor fishing offshore rather than to anything on the reserve. The count is conducted by 30 volunteers walking fixed transects over two days, a method unchanged in fifty years, which the reserve argues makes its long series more trustworthy than any single year's figure.
question: How many breeding pairs of terns did this year's count record?

passage: Thieves who tunneled into the strongroom of the Ostrander jewelry workshop over the weekend left behind the safe they had come for and escaped with almost nothing, the town police said on Monday, because the safe they spent hours opening had held only the shop's archive of paper repair records since a renovation in the spring. The workshop's stock, moved during the renovation to a newer safe bolted into the floor two rooms away, was untouched. The burglars entered through the cellar of the vacant fishmonger's next door, cutting a passage through 30 inches of shared brick wall with hand tools, work the police estimate took two nights. An alarm on the strongroom door never triggered because the door was never opened; the tunnel came up inside the room. The failed haul was discovered at 7:30 a.m. Monday by the shop's first arriving goldsmith. Owner Edda Ostrander said the old safe's contents, receipts and ledgers back to 1961, have modest value to historians and none to thieves. Police recovered a chisel, two drill bits, and a thermos at the scene, and are examining the fishmonger's rear lock, which shows no damage.
question: What did the safe the burglars opened actually contain?

passage: The chess tables in Halloran Park will be rebuilt in granite after the wooden originals, installed in 1983, were judged beyond repair, the parks department said on Wednesday. Regulars had petitioned for like-for-like oak replacements, arguing the wooden boards' worn squares were part of the park's character, but the department's assessment found rot in all nine tables and priced oak replacements at 41,000 dollars against 55,000 dollars for granite, with the granite expected to last at least four times as long. The department chose granite and will offset the higher price with a donation of 20,000 dollars from the estate of Gus Marbury, a retired postman who played at table four most afternoons for over thirty years and whose family asked that the new table four carry a small brass plate with his name. Two of the old oak boards, the least decayed, will be moved under the bandstand roof and kept for casual play. The park's summer blitz tournament, which drew 96 entrants last year, will be held at the community center during the eight weeks of work, which begins after the fair.
question: What material will the new chess tables be made of?
